question: Shared: prediction of MCI-to-AD progression in ADNI MCI, with MRI as the shared channel. P-199 (Lu et al., 2022) uses one baseline T1 image (3D ResNet-50, Med3D + MoCo) for 36-month conversion; P-168 (Ding et al., 2023) uses a multimodal model (neuropsychological tests + FreeSurfer volumes + demographics) that includes MRI, for conversion within 2 years of a month-24 index exam. Horizon, feature set, input timepoints and sample differ, which condition 1 allows.

figures.P-199: AUC 0.835 on a held-out 20% test set, no AUC interval printed (accuracy 0.819, bootstrap 95% CI 0.798-0.841). Test class sizes from the printed sensitivity 0.786 = 44/56 and specificity 0.850 = 51/60: 56 pMCI/60 sMCI (116, about 20% of 577). Hanley-McNeil: Q1 = 0.835/1.165 = 0.7167, Q2 = 2(0.835^2)/1.835 = 0.7599, SE = 0.0382, 95% CI [0.760, 0.910].
figures.P-168: Headline LSTM (five visits, all modalities) AUC 0.93 +/- 0.06 (fold SD), 10-fold CV over 347 participants (77 converters/270 non-converters). Hanley-McNeil: Q1 = 0.8692, Q2 = 0.8963, SE = 0.0206, 95% CI [0.890, 0.970]. Single-timepoint random forest, all modalities: 0.90, CI [0.853, 0.947]. MRI-only random forest (single 24-month timepoint): 0.85, SE 0.0287, CI [0.794, 0.906]. MRI-only LSTM: 0.86, CI [0.805, 0.915].

matched_figure_check: A matched figure exists and reconciles the pair. P-168 reports its result on P-199's condition of MRI-only input at a single timepoint: random forest on 24-month MRI measures, AUC 0.85 (MRI-only LSTM 0.86). P-199's 0.835 lies inside that figure's interval [0.794, 0.906], and 0.85 lies inside P-199's interval [0.760, 0.910]; the same holds for 0.86. On the headline figures the gap is beyond uncertainty (0.93 lies above P-199's upper bound 0.910, and 0.835 lies below P-168's lower bound 0.890). P-168's own data show that the gap comes from adding cognitive tests, demographics and longitudinal visits to MRI.
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply: 0.835 and 0.93 are below 0.97.
reason: The headline AUCs (0.835 vs 0.93) differ beyond uncertainty. But P-168 also reports MRI-only models (0.85 single timepoint, 0.86 longitudinal), and these agree with P-199's 0.835 in both directions. The papers' own figures dissolve the gap: it follows from P-168's added cognitive, demographic and longitudinal inputs, so condition 3 fails.
